crime: Every night, {WITCH_NAME} watched from the upper railing as a girl floated flowers from her basket on the courtyard fountain, one for each girl the prison had lost. When she was done, she always looked up and waved.
One night at half past nine, the girl called her down for the first time and put a flower in her hand. "When it's my turn, you'll float one for me, won't you?"
Long ago, at bedtime, {WITCH_NAME}'s mother had asked, "You'll remember me, won't you?" By morning she was gone. Ever since, every "remember me" had sounded like goodbye.

As the girl bent to set the first flower on the water, {WITCH_NAME} pushed her face under and held her there until she stopped moving. She laid her in the shadow under the tree, the basket beside her.

At a quarter to ten, as the other girls reached the upper railing on their way down, {WITCH_NAME} replayed last night's courtyard all around her. Looking down, they saw the girl alone at the fountain, floating flowers and waving up, while {WITCH_NAME} walked inside without her. She joined them on the stairs, and at ten she was locked in with them.

When the doors were unlocked, the prisoners found the girl lying drowned under the tree. In the trial court, they decided it must have happened at the fountain after a quarter to ten, while {WITCH_NAME} was on the stairs with them and then locked in.

Then one prisoner noticed the girl's basket. It was still full of fresh flowers, yet only last night's wilted ones floated on the fountain. They understood then: the girl they had watched floating flowers at a quarter to ten was a replay of the night before, playing out around {WITCH_NAME}, while the real one already lay beneath the tree.
fields.epitaph: Remembering her meant letting her go. She kept her instead.
fields.epithet: The girl who hears goodbye in "remember me"
execution: A giant flower rose on a tall stem to the very top of the trial court. She knelt inside its open blossom. One by one, its petals fell away, each drifting slowly down. When the flower was bare, it bowed and tipped her out, and she dropped head first onto the stone floor. She lay still among the fallen petals, the bare stem still bowed above her.

magic.name: The Room Remembers
magic.text: She can replay any past moment of the place she stands in, all around her.
